name: Working at Height
description: Score-based quiz covering fall-arrest classifications, edge protection distances, anchor point ratings and the hierarchy of fall-protection controls.

questions.description: Under the 'limited free fall' fall-arrest classification, what is the maximum free-fall distance permitted?
Fall protection or edge protection must be provided when an employee is required to work closer than what distance to the edge of a roof (or any point from which a fall is possible)?
In the hierarchy of fall-protection options, which control is the MOST preferred?
What minimum ultimate strength rating must an anchorage (or equivalent horizontal lifeline/rail) have for a full free-fall fall-arrest system limiting free fall to 2 m max?
True or False: if there is a possibility of the load of two persons being applied to a single anchor point, that anchor point should be able to withstand 21 kN.
In the hierarchy of risk controls (Elimination, Minimisation, Substitution, Isolation, Engineering controls, Administrative controls, PPE), which is considered the MOST effective?
What is the term for an assembly comprising a harness connected to an anchorage point (directly, or via a lanyard or pole strap) whose purpose is to arrest a fall?
Which of the following are valid ways to ELIMINATE the need to access a fall-risk area? (Select all that apply)
options: Relocate items requiring inspection or maintenance elsewhere
Provide an alternative means of access, e.g. a walkway
Wear a harness without any training
Work faster to reduce time exposed to the risk
correctAnswer: Relocate items requiring inspection or maintenance elsewhere
Provide an alternative means of access, e.g. a walkway
